newsitem.title: USA: CONSUMER COMFORT DIPS FROM RECORD HIGH - ABC/MONEY.
newsitem.headline: CONSUMER COMFORT DIPS FROM RECORD HIGH - ABC/MONEY.

text.p: Money Magazine/ABC News said on Wednesday their index of consumer comfort slipped two points to 11.0 in the week ended August 10, off from the prior week's all-time high of 13.0.
"Overall consumer confidence retreated from an all-time high this week as Americans expressed concern about spending money," Money Magazine and ABC News said.

However, Americans' confidence in the U.S. economy surged to an all-time high reading of 22 as "a record 61 percent of respondents said the economy is in good or excellent shape," a spokesman for the Money Magazine/ABC News survey said.
The survey also noted that "respondents' ratings of the current buying climate sank to a nine-week low. Only 43 percent said that now is a good time to spend money."

Regionally, confidence fell further in the West, retreated from a record high in the South, inched up in the Midwest and surged in the Northeast "where two-thirds of residents are optimistic about their finances," the survey added.
The Money/ABC News consumer comfort survey was started in 1985 and set a record low of -50 in February 1992.
The current poll, based on a random survey of 1,032 consumers nationwide, has a margin error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points.
